descriptionChirho: Adjective describing what belongs to or comes from an earlier time, used attributively and substantively. Applied to persons of old ('the ancients' to whom it was said: Matt 5:21, 33), to ancient prophets risen (Luke 9:8, 19), to ancient days and early decisions (Acts 15:7, 21), to the primeval world (2 Pet 2:5 'ancient world'), to the ancient serpent/Satan (Rev 12:9, 20:2), to old things that pass away in Christ (2 Cor 5:17), and to an early disciple Mnason (Acts 21:16). Multilingual glosses uniformly render 'ancient/old' (arb: قديم, deu: alt, heb: קדמון/עתיקים, hin: प्राचीन/पुराना, kor: 옛, spa: antiguo).
